title: Governor of Rhode Island

context.text: Incumbent Democratic Gov. Dan McKee sought a second full term but lost the Sept. 9, 2026 Democratic primary to Helena Foulkes, 62.5% to 37.5% (81,314 votes to 48,872). It was the first time since 1994 that a Rhode Island governor lost renomination.
Republican primary (Sept. 9, 2026): Aaron Guckian defeated Elaine Pelino 50.6% to 49.4% (11,691 to 11,432 votes); Pelino requested a recount, which did not change the outcome.
Ken Block, founder of the Moderate Party of Rhode Island, is running as an independent; Jasjit Gotra and C.D. Reynolds also qualified for the November ballot as independents.
The lieutenant governor is a separate office on the 2026 ballot, with its own candidates.

candidates.name: Helena Foulkes
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Sept. 9 Democratic primary, defeating incumbent Gov. Dan McKee 62.5% to 37.5%.
candidates.currentRole: Former CVS executive; former CEO of Hudson's Bay Company

priorities.text: Housing: dedicate millionaire's-tax revenue to a revolving loan fund she says would produce 20,000 new homes in eight years.
Accountability in state government, including a plan to create an Office of Safety and Accountability at RIDOT after the Washington Bridge closure, and ethics reform.
Jobs and affordability: plans on child care and transportation, career and technical education, and energy costs.

positions.summary: Proposes dedicating revenue from a millionaire's tax to a revolving loan fund for housing construction.
Said at the Oct. 7 debate that ICE would not be welcome in Rhode Island under her governorship.
positions.quote: ICE is not welcome when I am governor.

positions.summary: Said at the Oct. 7 debate that she supports allowing transgender girls to participate in girls' sports.

candidates.researchNotes: No official record items are included. Ran in the 2022 Democratic primary for governor (lost).

candidates.name: Aaron Guckian
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Sept. 9 Republican primary over Elaine Pelino by 259 votes; a recount did not change the result.
candidates.currentRole: Former head of the Rhode Island Dental Association

priorities.text: Lower taxes and fees: he describes Rhode Island as 'the state of toos' with too many taxes, fees and speed cameras and high electricity bills.
priorities.quote: I'm here because we're the state of toos. Too many taxes, too many fees, too many speed cameras.

priorities.text: Opposes a millionaire's tax and the return of Rhode Island's truck tolls; would cut the tax on second homes.
Says he would work with the Trump administration to bring funding to Rhode Island.
priorities.quote: I look forward to working with the administration and President Trump.

positions.summary: Opposes the millionaire's tax Foulkes proposes for housing, calling it more spending.
positions.quote: It's more spending. More spending. It doesn't work.

positions.summary: Asked at the Oct. 7 debate whether ICE would be welcome in Rhode Island, he said yes.
positions.quote: Yes. We need to get the bad actors out.

positions.summary: Said at the Oct. 7 debate that he opposes allowing transgender girls to participate in girls' sports.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website was reachable in this pass. No official record items are included.

candidates.name: Ken Block
candidates.ballotNote: Independent; qualified for the ballot outside the party primaries.
candidates.currentRole: Founder, Moderate Party of Rhode Island; former president of RI Taxpayers

priorities.text: Accountability in state government, pointing to the Washington Bridge closure and failed technology projects.
Cutting state fees on energy bills.

positions.summary: Said at the Oct. 7 debate that he has always been pro-choice.
positions.quote: I am pro-choice, I have always been pro-choice.

positions.summary: Said ICE operations cause fear and that there is a humane way to enforce immigration laws.
positions.quote: There is a humane way to enforce our laws.

positions.summary: Said at the Oct. 7 debate that he opposes allowing transgender girls to participate in girls' sports.

candidates.researchNotes: No official record items are included; his background is as a party founder and taxpayer-group leader.

candidates.name: Jasjit Gotra

priorities.text: Make Rhode Island profitable: run government like a business, publish a state profit-and-loss statement and hold every agency to a budget.
Honor every pension, including full funding of teachers' and firefighters' pensions.
Eliminate the state tax on Social Security within the first two years.
Cut red tape for businesses and bring AI tools into every classroom.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from the Policies page of his campaign site (governorgotra.com), loaded with a headless browser. No abortion, gun, immigration or minimum-wage positions found there.

researchNotes: The lieutenant governor is listed as a separate office with its own candidates. Record sections are empty because no officeholder record was researched. Ballotpedia was blocked from this environment (bot challenge), and the Board of Elections and Secretary of State candidate lists could not be loaded. The five-candidate slate (Foulkes, Guckian, Block, Gotra, Reynolds) is confirmed by two independent sources, NPR/New England Public Media and The Green Papers, in addition to the Wikipedia race page, which is also the source for primary results. Foulkes's and Guckian's positions rest mostly on NBC 10 coverage of the Oct. 7 debate and on Foulkes's campaign plans page; Guckian's campaign site was not reachable. Official lists checked again on 2026-10-19: the Board of Elections upcoming-elections page lists only the Nov. 3 date, and the Secretary of State's vote.sos.ri.gov candidate pages are blocked by a bot challenge, so the slate remains news-only (NEPM and The Green Papers). Update: Gotra's positions come from his campaign site's Policies page; he is now 'basic'. Reynolds has no public issue statements found.
